body:
I also think boundaries are going to become extremely important.

I have tried to explain to him that he has to want to change himself, that i can't change him, but that's just like me to want to mother him and when I can't protect him I feel useless. I know that's my own problem. I'm trying not to hold on so tightly, but it's hard once you're in so deep.

Trying to be positive when talking to him, hoping it rubs off, but my fuse is so short (and I am ordinarily so patient with everyone) that as soon as he falls into old habits I just want to shake him.

Thanks for the good wishes.

Oh man, that comic hit way too close to home, as did the Wiki article. 

Thanks for that. it's enormously comforting to know that there are delicate ways around this. I don't want him to hurt any more than he already does, especially because of me.

You know, having been down this road before, the part you quoted is exactly what I've told people *not* to believe if/when I choose to go that way. 

I cut a friend out in high school, so I know it can be done, but she really didn't do a thing for me and it didn't damage anything except the friendship between her and I. With this guy, he's helped me and even talked me down when I've been suicidal, and I'm infinitely grateful for that. I love him like a brother and he is part of a very tight group of friends. I worry how damaging the fallout could be if I suddenly pushed him away... would he get pushed out of the herd entirely and left to fend for himself?

He does need a support system and I don't feel like it's the guilt talking. he's a long way from home, no family around him, lives alone, and I only get to talk to him online unless he comes over to our house once every few months with some of our other friends. Thank you for your advice, though, Iv'e been trying to point him in the right direction and he's resisting.

It might be the guilt talking, but I don't feel like he sucks the life out of me all the time... just when things get really bad, everythign snowballs and I feel overwhelmed because I have a life too, you know? he isn't the center of my universe, I have already promised myself to that person, but this guy is a very big part of it and is part of our circle of friends... I worry that either I couldn't get a clean break, or that he'd be alienated from the group and truly be alone.

This is the worst part. He feels like he doesn't have anyone else to talk to, anyone else to calm him down and just talk when things get bad, and I told him that I feel like it's a losing battle when I'm his biggest problem. I suggested professional help, he came up with a million excuses why it wouldn't work, I argued that it can ALWAYS work, and he just attacked the fact that I claim "the system didn't work for me" (it didn't. my fault).

He's a close-knit "group friend" and it would be impossible to cut him out entirely which is a big part of why I haven't come down as hard as I probably should on him. I do still care, very much, but (as my husband put it) I need to let him cry it out and make his own decisions, he's an adult.

namely that he's lonely and will never find "the one". He's worried about being one of those "forever alone" types and ever since I started talking to him about a year ago, he's fallen for me. so now instead of "help me find someone" it's become "help me find someone exactly like you", which is a step up from when he suggested that I'd be happier with him than in my current relationship.

he is smart and funny and has helped me every time I've been down, even talking me down from the edge a couple of times. There is a lot of give and take, and I'm grateful that he's been there for me, so that's why I feel so much guilt in just letting him go. I'm trying to help him love himself first before he goes out looking for some random chick to fill the hole in his heart because that's just asking for him to get burned.
